Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- 31-year-old woman with 6-day history of dysuria, foul-smelling urine, intermittent suprapubic pain (7/10), and visible hematuria spots. No fever, flank pain, or systemic symptoms.  
- Most consistent with acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis (high likelihood).  
- Differential considerations: urethritis secondary to STI (medium likelihood; limited sexual history), urinary tract calculi (low–medium likelihood; hematuria but no colicky flank pain).  
- Plan (as per transcript):  
  • Empiric 3-day course of antibiotics (drug/dose not documented) sent to nominated pharmacy.  
  • Advice to increase oral fluids to 2.5–3 L/day, consider cranberry juice, and over-the-counter urinary alkalinising sachets.  
  • Obtain home thermometer; monitor temperature.  
  • Safety-netting: seek review if pain worsens, develops fever, flank pain, difficulty voiding, or recurrent episodes.  
  • No immediate investigations ordered; will consider further work-up (urinalysis/culture, STI screening) if symptoms persist or recur.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Acute uncomplicated bacterial cystitis – High likelihood: classic dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, mild hematuria; no systemic or upper-tract signs.  
2. Urethritis (Chlamydia/Gonorrhoea) – Moderate likelihood: dysuria ± hematuria can mimic cystitis; sexual history limited; no discharge reported.  
3. Urinary tract calculi – Low–moderate likelihood: hematuria and abdominal pain possible but absence of flank colic lowers probability.
